sources.entry: Checklists: a stupidly simple but valuable operational gift

summary.name: Checklists: an operational gift
summary.one_liner: A BuzzFeed tech blog post arguing for writing checklists for production operations and incidents, with guidance on checklist format, back-out plans, and roles during execution.
use_cases: Planning a production deployment or migration with no downtime
Writing a rollback plan for a risky change
Coordinating responders during a production incident
Running a team operation with clear driver, executor and watcher roles
Peer-reviewing an operational procedure before execution
summary.what_it_does: The post argues that every production operation, from trivial to crisis, should have a written checklist reviewed by peers. It gives concrete format rules: use numbered steps, avoid sub-lists, include full copy-pasteable commands, name the responsible person for each step, link merged pull requests, and add logical breakpoints. It stresses writing a back-out plan and marking the point of no return. It also describes operational roles (driver, executors, watchers, and an "OMFG Officer" who makes executive calls) and an execution flow using a dedicated chat channel and voice call.
notable: Defines driver, executor, watcher and OMFG Officer roles for live operations
Requires a back-out checklist held to the same standard as the rollout checklist
Recommends marking the point of no return in the rollout plan
Advises not modifying the checklist mid-operation unless it is do-or-die
caveats: Written as an opinion/advice essay; it is a blog post, not a tool or product
Some advice is informal (e.g., the OMFG Officer role is described as largely decorative)
